question: What is the primary purpose of using a partograph during labor?

options.A: To replace the need for physical abdominal examinations
options.B: To provide an early visual warning when labor becomes abnormal
options.C: To record only the medications given after delivery
options.D: To calculate the exact date and time of conception

explanation: The partograph is designed as a graphical tool to track labor progress and give early signals if something is going wrong. [learn more](BMP212_U2_T6#BMP212_U2_T6_h1)

question: Why is the partograph particularly valuable in busy healthcare facilities?

options.A: It removes the requirement to monitor the fetal heart rate
options.B: It acts as a clear communication tool between different shifts of staff
options.C: It completely automates the delivery process without human effort
options.D: It guarantees that no complications will ever happen during birth

explanation: A graphical chart allows incoming midwives to see at a glance how labor has progressed over time. [learn more](BMP212_U2_T6#BMP212_U2_T6_h1)

question: Which of the following parameters is NOT recorded in the fetal condition section of the partograph?
explanation: Maternal blood pressure belongs to the maternal condition section, while heart rate and liquor status belong to the fetal section. [learn more](BMP212_U2_T6#BMP212_U2_T6_h2)

question: Where on the partograph is the graphical tracking of cervical dilation recorded?
explanation: Cervical dilation and head descent are core measurements tracked under the progress of labor part of the chart. [learn more](BMP212_U2_T6#BMP212_U2_T6_h2)

question: At what centimeter of cervical dilatation does the alert line on the partograph traditionally begin?
explanation: The active phase of labor is recognized to start at 4 cm, which is where the alert line begins. [learn more](BMP212_U2_T6#BMP212_U2_T6_h3)

question: What is a key action when a woman's labor progress crosses to the right of the alert line?

options.A: Administer a massive dose of pain relief medication
options.B: Stop all monitoring because normal labor has now concluded
options.C: Perform an immediate emergency Cesarean section in the same room
options.D: Evaluate the cause of slow progress and prepare for potential transfer

explanation: Reaching the alert line warns of slow progress, prompting assessment and preparations for moving the patient if needed. [learn more](BMP212_U2_T6#BMP212_U2_T6_h3)

question: How many hours to the right of the alert line is the action line placed on the standard partograph?
explanation: The action line is positioned exactly four hours to the right of the alert line to allow a clear window for warning before decisive intervention is mandatory. [learn more](BMP212_U2_T6#BMP212_U2_T6_h4)

question: A laboring woman's cervical dilatation curve crosses the action line on her partograph. What does this indicate?

options.A: The partograph was filled out incorrectly and should be discarded
options.B: Immediate medical intervention or delivery decision is required
options.C: The baby will be born naturally within the next ten minutes
options.D: No action is needed as long as the mother feels comfortable

explanation: Crossing the action line means delay is significant and active medical management or surgical delivery must be initiated. [learn more](BMP212_U2_T6#BMP212_U2_T6_h4)

question: Why is delayed plotting on a partograph hours after examinations take place discouraged?

options.A: It changes the fetal heart rate to an abnormal rhythm
options.B: It makes the paper chart look untidy and difficult to read
options.C: It uses up too much ink in the clinic's ballpoint pens
options.D: It hides delayed labor progress and delays necessary life-saving interventions

explanation: Delayed entry masks real-time problems, meaning the alert and action lines will not give their timely warning. [learn more](BMP212_U2_T6#BMP212_U2_T6_h5)

question: When interpreting labor progress, why must the midwife observe fetal head descent together with cervical dilatation?

options.A: To confirm that the baby is actually moving down the birth canal despite dilation
options.B: To decide whether the mother needs an enema
options.C: To calculate the exact birth weight of the infant before delivery
options.D: To determine the blood type of the mother

explanation: A cervix can dilate while the head stays high, which is a major sign of cephalopelvic disproportion. [learn more](BMP212_U2_T6#BMP212_U2_T6_h5)
